output_json.patch_notes:
Added a private static helper `checkDestinationInsideTargetDir(File targetDir, String entryName, File destFile)` in ZipUtil.java that computes canonical paths for both targetDir and the candidate destination file and throws ZipException if the destination does not equal or fall strictly under the target directory. Wired this helper into the three sink locations named in the alert:
1. Unpacker#process — `new File(outputDir, name)` now passed through the check before use in forceMkdir/copy.
2. BackslashUnpacker#process — each intermediate segment File in the directory-creation loop, the final backslash-split destFile, and the top-level (non-backslash) destFile are all now checked.
3. Unwraper#process — `new File(outputDir, name)` (post root-unwrapping/name-mapping) is now checked.
Also added three JUnit regression tests to ZipUtilTest.java (testUnpackPreventsZipSlip, testUnpackBackslashesPreventsZipSlip, testUnwrapPreventsZipSlip) that build a malicious zip with a traversal entry name ("../evil-escaped.txt", "..\\evil-escaped.txt", "root/../evil-escaped.txt" respectively) and assert a ZipException is thrown and no file is written outside the destination directory. Full test suite run (119 tests) shows only one failure, testPreserveWriteFlag in FilePermissionsTest, which was confirmed via git stash to fail identically on the unpatched baseline (pre-existing, environment-related — likely due to running as root in the build container — unrelated to this change).
output_json.risk_notes: Low risk: the change only adds a validation guard before existing file-write logic; it does not alter behavior for well-formed (non-traversal) zip entries, since canonical destination paths for legitimate entries always fall under the canonical target directory. Entries that previously escaped the target directory now cause a ZipException (a RuntimeException already used elsewhere in this codebase for zip-processing errors) instead of silently writing files outside the sandbox — this is an intentional, necessary behavior change to close the vulnerability and matches how the exploiter's PoV expected a fix to behave (unpack() throwing rather than silently succeeding). Callers that were relying on the previously-vulnerable escape behavior (unlikely for legitimate use) would now see an exception; this is the correct/expected outcome for a security fix. Symlink-based escapes (writing through a pre-existing symlink inside outputDir) are a separate, deeper issue noted by the exploiter as out of scope for this PoV/alert and are not addressed by canonical-path containment checks; consider a follow-up if that threat model applies.
output_json.summary: Fixed the Zip Slip / path traversal vulnerability (CWE-22) in org.zeroturnaround.zip.ZipUtil by adding a shared containment check (checkDestinationInsideTargetDir) that resolves each extraction target's canonical path and verifies it stays inside the caller-supplied output directory before any directory creation or file write occurs. This root-cause fix is applied at all three vulnerable sinks identified in the alert: Unpacker#process (line ~1152, used by all unpack(File/InputStream, File, ...) overloads), BackslashUnpacker#process (both the per-segment directory-creation loop and the final file write, covering backslash-separated traversal like "..\\evil.txt"), and Unwraper#process (line ~1260, used by unwrap(...) and root-shaving unpack variants). Any entry (file or directory type) whose resolved path escapes the target directory now throws a ZipException instead of silently writing outside the sandbox — this also blocks absolute-path entry names since new File(targetDir, absoluteChild) is still checked against the canonical target dir prefix.
